AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To assess the effectiveness and tolerability of tapentadol sustained release (SR) following its introduction to the Australian private market.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: A retrospective audit of routine clinical practice with data collection beginning 2 months after the first tapentadol SR prescription.

AbstractText.Label: PATIENTS
AbstractText.content: Fifty patients who were prescribed tapentadol SR as part of routine clinical management at the pain clinic.

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTIONS
AbstractText.content: Trial of tapentadol SR with subsequent dose titration if the patient was satisfied with or tolerant of the medication.

AbstractText.Label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
AbstractText.content: Patient-reported pain outcome, side effects, medication adherence, and concomitant analgesic medications.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Sixty-eight percent of patients reported major reductions in pain. Seventy-two percent of patients tolerated and adhered to treatment and 76 percent reported no side effects. Pain outcome was independent of pain type and prior opioid exposure; however, patients taking tapentadol in combination were more likely to report a positive outcome (Pearson χ(2) = 9.867, n = 46, p = 0.0072).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Tapentadol was effective and generally well tolerated in the majority of patients for neuropathic, nociceptive and mixed pain types and this was regardless of prior opioid use.
